newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakhstan to shortlist 3 bidders in telecoms deal.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhstan to shortlist 3 bidders in telecoms deal.

text.p: Kazakhstan will shortlist three bidders for a stake in Kazakh telecoms monopoly NAK Kazakhtelekom next week, a privatisation official said on Wednesday.

"Next week the number of participants in the tender will be reduced to three, with whom we will closely work to finalise the sell-off," Birzhan Madiyev, in charge of individual projects privatisation at the finance ministry's state property department, told Reuters.
Kazakhtelekom chairman Serik Burkitbayev has said previously he expected the winner of the tender to be named in April.
Last week representatives of the government opened envelopes with investment offers from seven companies.

The bidders included Germany's Siemens AG, Alcatel Alstrom SA unit Alcatel Sel AG, Korea's Daewoo and Hanwha, Malaysia's Usaha Tegas Sdn Bnd and Kazakhstan Asset Management Ltd, and Kaztel Investment Group registered in the British Virgin Islands.
Madiyev said Alcatel had later joined forces with Kaztel Investment Group, while Kazakhstan Asset Management had fallen out of the number of the tender bidders.
The tender for the right to buy a 40 percent stake in Kazakhtelekom was announced in January this year after a government deal with Germany's Deutsche Telekom AG fell through.

Burkitbayev has said previously the telecoms monopoly, where 90 percent of shares are state-owned and 10 percent belong to its employees, needed investment of around 1.5 billion marks ($897.8 million).

Kazakhtelekom wants an investor to share responsibility for debts of 420 million marks for a credit granted in 1992 by Germany's investment agency Kreditanstalt fur Wiederaufbau which must be repaid by 2004.

The monopoly wants to bring the number of telephone lines in the Central Asian state with a population of 16.9 million people to five million from today's 2.1 million. It also wants to use Kazakhstan's geographical position in the centre of Eurasia to become a communications hub linking Europe and Asia.
